title: Pacific loon breeding-state resight histories of 50 colour-banded adults, National Petroleum Reserve-Alaska, 2011-2014
creator: Uher-Koch, Brian D.; Schmutz, Joel A.
citation: Uher-Koch, B., and Schmutz, J., 2019, Pacific (Gavia pacifica) and Yellow-billed Loon (G. adamsii) mark-resight encounter history data; National Petroleum Reserve-Alaska, 2011-2014: U.S. Geological Survey data release, https://doi.org/10.5066/F7HH6J9C.
abstract: Annual resighting of colour-banded pacific loons on their breeding territories on the Arctic Coastal Plain of the National Petroleum Reserve-Alaska (Chipp North and Chipp South study areas), 2011-2014, recording whether each marked loon was seen on its territory and, if so, whether it was a non-breeder, an unsuccessful breeder or a successful breeder (chicks surviving three weeks), to estimate territory retention and apparent survival.
samplingProtocol: Loons were caught on their territories (suspended dive-net), colour-banded and measured; each summer territories were searched from shore with spotting scopes, binoculars or telephoto cameras and banded birds identified, and nesting outcome recorded.

stateCodes.3: successful breeder (chicks survived at least 3 weeks)

geographicCoverage.description: Chipp River area, Arctic Coastal Plain, National Petroleum Reserve-Alaska, USA

notShipped.other_species: the yellow-billed loons in the same file ship as the sibling table

notes: Histories left-padded to four years (the deposited numbers lost leading zeros). Adults of unknown age: rows from 2011 (E4.4), y = 0 before capture.
